title: The stuck watch reads pi-CLI session transcripts for a runner that has none
body:
The subprocess supervisor's activity watch still reads the pi CLI's session transcripts (LastTranscriptEvent's `pi` case) for the runner now named `pi` — which is the Node pi-durable host and writes its conversation to the attempt's SQLite, not to pi's session files. The watch still decides correctly (tool-process CPU, worktree and branch moves carry it; the harness's own partial commits every ~100ms keep the runner's CPU moving during streaming), but the evidence sentence a stuck nudge carries now always says "no session transcript could be read", which misleads an operator reading where a live worker's progress lives. The honest signal is the storage file's mtime — commits are the heartbeat — or y03's commit-stream view.
evidence: internal/exec/subprocess/activity.go LastTranscriptEvent (case "pi"), and its Evidence sentence; the storage is internal/exec/subprocess/workerconfig.go fileWorkerStorage
